passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis is intended to help the reader understand the Company, our financial condition and results of operations and our present business environment. It should be read together with our consolidated financial statements and related notes contained elsewhere in this Annual Report. The following discussion and analysis contain certain financial measures that are not required by, or presented in accordance with, accounting principles generally accepted in the U.S. (“GAAP”). We believe these non-GAAP financial measures provide meaningful supplemental information about our operating performance and liquidity. Information regarding reconciliations of and the rationale for these measures is discussed in “Non-GAAP Reconciliations” below. The following includes a comparison of our consolidated results of operations for fiscal years 2025 and 2024. For a comparison of our consolidated results of operations for fiscal years 2024 and 2023, see Item 7 of Part II, “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations”, of our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 28, 2024, filed with the SEC on February 13, 2025. Overview At US Foods, we strive to inspire and empower chefs and foodservice operators to bring great food experiences to consumers. This mission is supported by our strategy of WE HELP YOU MAKE IT ® , which is centered on bringing three key elements to the forefront for our customers; (1) More Quality products, including our large portfolio of Exclusive Brands, (2) More Tools, centering on our MOXē ® business platform, and lastly, (3) More Deliveries, enabled by our traditional broadline services, Pronto ® program and convenient delivery options. We operate as one business with standardized business processes, shared systems infrastructure, and an organizational model that optimizes national scale with local execution, allowing us to manage our business as a single operating segment. We have centralized activities where scale matters and our local field structure focuses on customer-facing activities. Operating Metrics Case growth —Case growth, by customer type (e.g., independent restaurants) is reported as of a point in time. Customers periodically are reclassified, based on changes in size or other characteristics, and when those changes occur, the respective customer’s historical volume is included within the new classification. Organic growth —Organic growth includes growth from operating businesses that have been reflected in our results of operations for at least 12 months. Fiscal Year 2025 Highlights Financial Highlights —Total case volume increased 1.0% compared to the prior year driven by a 3.3% increase in independent restaurant case volume, a 4.4% increase in healthcare volume and a 2.9% increase in hospitality volume, partially offset by a 3.5% decrease in chain volume. Total organic case volume increased 0.4% in fiscal year 2025, which includes 2.7% organic independent restaurant case volume growth. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: We are subject to many risks and uncertainties. Some of these risks and uncertainties, including those described below, may cause our business, financial condition and results of operations to vary, and they may materially or adversely affect our financial performance. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Other risks and uncertainties, which are not currently known to us or which we currently believe are immaterial, may also materially or adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry An economic downturn, public health crisis, and/or other factors affecting consumer spending and confidence, may reduce the amount of food prepared away from home, which may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations. The U.S. foodservice distribution industry is sensitive to national, regional and local economic conditions. An uneven level of general U.S. economic activity, uncertainty in the financial markets, inflation, and supply chain disruptions could have an adverse impact on consumer confidence and discretionary spending. A decline in economic activity or the frequency and amount spent by consumers for food prepared away from home, as well as other macroenvironmental factors that could decrease general consumer confidence (including deteriorating economic conditions, heightened volatility in the financial markets, tariffs, inflationary pressure, an uncertain geopolitical environment, trade policies and supply chain disruptions, such as those the global economy is currently facing), may negatively impact our business, financial condition and results of operations. The extent of any such effects on our business, financial condition and results of operations depends in part on the magnitude and duration of such conditions, which cannot be predicted at this time. Our business is a low-margin business, and our profitability and results of operations are directly affected by cost deflation or inflation, volatile food costs and other factors. The U.S. foodservice distribution industry is characterized by relatively high inventory turnover with relatively low profit margins. Volatile food costs have a direct impact on our industry. Our inability to quickly respond to inflationary and deflationary cost pressures could have a material adverse impact on our business, financial condition, or results of operations. We make a significant portion of our sales at prices that are based on the cost of products we sell, plus a margin percentage or markup. As a result, our profit levels may be negatively affected during periods of product cost deflation, even though our gross profit percentage may remain relatively constant. Prolonged periods of product cost inflation, or periods of rapid inflation, may negatively impact our results of operations as a result of decreased discretionary consumer spending. Such inflation may also reduce our profit margins and earnings if there is a lag between when costs increase and when we are able to pass on all or a portion of such product cost increases along to customers. credit_strengths.text: US Foods is a scaled broadline foodservice distributor with revenue rising steadily across the last three fiscal years, and operating income improving in each period. Case growth in independent restaurants, healthcare and hospitality offset chain weakness, supporting the view that the top-line trajectory is durable rather than cyclical. Operating margin remains thin, consistent with the low-margin distribution model, but the direction of earnings is positive.

Operating cash flow covers capital expenditure comfortably, leaving free cash flow that is substantial relative to reported debt. This internally generated liquidity is the primary support for the capital structure, and it has strengthened over the three-year trend. The company also maintains a current ratio modestly above one, indicating adequate near-term working capital coverage.

key_risks.text: The risk-factor passage highlights that foodservice distribution is a low-margin business directly exposed to volatile food costs, with a lag between cost inflation and pass-through to customers. Prolonged or rapid inflation could compress margins and earnings, while deflation may reduce profit levels even if gross margin percentage holds. This cost volatility is a structural earnings risk for US Foods.

Leverage sits above the sector median, and the indicative financial risk profile is significant. The debt stack includes a meaningful short-term borrowing component alongside long-term maturities, with a large portion falling due in the third year. Refinancing this maturity wall at higher rates would pressure interest coverage, which already trails the sector median. Shareholder distributions absorb most free cash flow, limiting deleveraging capacity.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is adequate but below the sector median, and the indicative cash-flow tier is weaker than the leverage tier. Free cash flow to debt is modest relative to sector norms, meaning debt service depends on maintaining operating cash flow. A decline in EBITDA or cash flow would narrow headroom toward the next threshold, so the servicing profile is sensitive to earnings volatility.

Cash on hand is minimal relative to debt, so the company relies on refinancing and operating cash flow rather than balance-sheet liquidity. The maturity profile is manageable in the near term but concentrates in the third year, requiring either refinancing or cash generation. Given the low cash balance, a refinancing disruption would be more consequential than for peers with larger liquidity buffers.

overall_credit_view.text: US Foods presents a stable but leveraged credit profile. Revenue and operating income are trending upward, and operating cash flow comfortably funds capital expenditure. However, leverage is above the sector median, interest coverage is below it, and the indicative financial risk profile is significant. The company's low-margin, cost-sensitive business model adds cyclical earnings risk.

Our forward view is that credit quality hinges on sustaining operating cash flow while managing the third-year maturity concentration and shareholder distributions that absorb most free cash flow. Deleveraging would require EBITDA growth or reduced buybacks. We would monitor food-cost inflation and refinancing conditions as key swing factors. This assessment is analyst judgement, not a rating.

credit_strengths.text: US Foods 是一家具規模的broadline餐飲服務分銷商，過去三個財政年度收入穩步上升，各期營運收入均見改善。獨立餐廳、醫療及酒店業的個案增長抵銷了連鎖業務的疲弱，支持了收入軌跡具持久性而非周期性的觀點。營運利潤率仍然偏薄，與低利潤率分銷模式一致，但盈利方向正面。
營運現金流足以輕鬆覆蓋資本開支，留下相對於報告債務而言可觀的自由現金流。此內部產生的流動性是資本結構的主要支撐，並在三年趨勢中有所增強。公司亦維持略高於一的流動比率，顯示短期營運資金覆蓋充足。

key_risks.text: 風險因素段落強調，餐飲服務分銷是一項低利潤率業務，直接暴露於波動的食品成本，成本通脹與轉嫁予客戶之間存在時滯。持續或快速的通脹可能壓縮利潤率及盈利，而通縮即使毛利率百分比保持不變，亦可能降低利潤水平。此成本波動對US Foods而言是一項結構性盈利風險。
槓桿高於行業中位數，而指示性財務風險狀況屬重大。債務結構包括一項有意義的短期借款組成部分，以及長期到期債務，其中一大部分於第三年到期。以較高利率為此到期牆再融資將對利息覆蓋率構成壓力，而該比率已落後於行業中位數。股東分派吸收大部分自由現金流，限制了去槓桿能力。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率充足但低於行業中位數，而指示性現金流級別弱於槓桿級別。自由現金流對債務比率相對於行業常規而言屬溫和，意味著償債依賴於維持營運現金流。EBITDA或現金流下降將收窄邁向下一個門檻的空間，因此償債狀況對盈利波動敏感。
手頭現金相對於債務而言極少，因此公司依賴再融資及營運現金流，而非資產負債表流動性。到期結構在短期內可控，但集中於第三年，需要再融資或現金產生。鑑於現金餘額偏低，再融資中斷的後果將比擁有較大流動性緩衝的同業更為嚴重。

overall_credit_view.text: US Foods呈現穩定但槓桿化的信用狀況。收入及營運收入呈上升趨勢，營運現金流輕鬆為資本開支提供資金。然而，槓桿高於行業中位數，利息覆蓋率低於該水平，而指示性財務風險狀況屬重大。公司低利潤率、對成本敏感的商業模式增加了周期性盈利風險。
我們的前瞻觀點是，信用質素取決於維持營運現金流，同時管理第三年到期集中度及吸收大部分自由現金流的股東分派。去槓桿將需要EBITDA增長或減少回購。我們將監測食品成本通脹及再融資條件作為關鍵擺動因素。此評估屬分析師判斷，並非評級。
